title: Last freedom-class LCS USS CLEVELAND hits tug during launch, April 15
description:
Last freedom-class LCS hits tug during launch
U.S. Navy confirms that USS CLEVELAND made contact with an assist tug during her side launch. On Saturday April 15, Fincantieri's Marinette yard launched the Freedom-class Littoral Combat Ship USS CLEVELAND, the last of the 16-vessel series and one of the six that the U.S. Navy desires to keep in its long-range fleet plan. CLEVELAND was also the last vessel that Marinette will put in the water with a dramatic side-launch, as it is installing a ship-lift for gentler lowering away. 
Video of the launch ceremony captured by bystanders appears to show that USS CLEVELAND washed the back deck and wheelhouse of an assist tug with the wave created by her entry into the water, bucking the tug's bow upwards and pushing the smaller boat across the channel. Two videos appear to show a tug crewmember running forward, away from the back deck, before the wave washes over the stern.
The U.S. Navy confirmed that USS CLEVELAND made contact with the tug during launch, and the LCS sustained minor damage due to the impact. “No personnel injuries occurred, but there was limited damage,"
